Resource Metadata Extensions, line 144: r3_vocabularies keys MUST be vocabulary URIs, urn:aauth:vocabulary: ones for the standard vocabularies

Resource Token Extensions, lines 497-503: a Resource token carrying R3 information MUST include both r3_uri and r3_s256 (also checked: Resource iss, and aud naming the AS in four-party or the PS in three-party access, line 499)

R3 Document, line 448: the Resource MUST require a valid HTTP Message Signature on requests to R3 document URIs and MUST reject requests not signed by the entitled AS or PS; agents cannot fetch R3 documents

R3 Document Access Restriction, lines 729-734: the Resource MUST reject any signer, identified by id, that is not the AS in the Resource token's aud or the PS in its ps; any other signer MUST be rejected
Content Addressing, lines 486-488: r3_s256 is the SHA-256 of the bytes as served; the Resource MUST serve those exact bytes on every request for the same r3_uri, here to each entitled signer
Fields, lines 469-471: vocabulary is REQUIRED and MUST match a vocabulary advertised in r3_vocabularies; operations is REQUIRED
Operations Spanning Multiple Definitions, line 435: the Resource MUST reference a single R3 document that covers all of the requested operations

Operation Validation, line 748: the Resource MUST validate declared operations against its authoritative definition before issuing a Resource token; an operation outside it, or a vocabulary the Resource does not advertise (line 412), gets no Resource token
Grant Enforcement, line 758: Resources MUST enforce r3_granted and r3_per_call and MUST reject API calls that match an operation in neither claim
Resource Enforcement, step 1 (line 625): a call matching r3_granted is served; the 2xx status and the operation echo are the launcher's

Verification (Server), lines 2242-2250, applied to the R3 document endpoint: any failure MUST result in a 401 with the appropriate Signature-Error; missing signature fields (step 1) and a signature that does not verify (step 7) are invalid_signature

Grant Enforcement, line 758: operations in r3_per_call MUST trigger an AAuth-Requirement before being served; the challenge is a 401 or 202 whose Resource token references a proposal, not the class document, names the AS in aud and the presented Auth token in presented_jti (Flow, step 1, line 675; line 499)

Proposal Document, lines 643-645: a per-call proposal's operations (REQUIRED) is the single r3_per_call operation invoked and its parameters (REQUIRED) carry the call's concrete parameters; it is content-addressed like a class document (line 637)
Flow, step 3, line 677: on the 401 retry the Resource MUST verify the presented parameters match the approved proposal and MUST reject the call if anything differs; nothing is executed
Flow, step 4, line 678: a Resource MUST NOT execute more than one invocation under one per-call Auth token; the launcher counts its own executions
Issuer Processing, lines 543-546: an issuer receiving a Resource token carrying r3_uri and r3_s256 MUST fetch the R3 document at r3_uri
R3 Document Access Restriction, line 729: a party fetching r3_uri MUST sign the request as a server in its own right, under the jwks_uri scheme with id set to its issuer (aauth-person.json for a PS)
Issuer Processing, step 3, line 547: if the SHA-256 of the bytes received does not match r3_s256, the issuer MUST reject the Resource token
Hash Verification, line 740: a party that fetches an R3 document MUST verify r3_s256 against it before using it; with no document fetched there is nothing verified to grant from

Issuer Processing, step 6 (line 550), and Auth Token Extensions, lines 569-571: the issued Auth token MUST include r3_uri and r3_s256 of the document and r3_granted (REQUIRED), whose operations are drawn from that document (line 617)
Resource Token Extensions, line 530: when a Resource token carries both scope and R3 claims, the Auth token's issuer MUST enforce both independently; the granted scope is the host's
Issuer Processing, lines 543-546: in four-party access the AS is the Auth-token issuer and MUST fetch the R3 document at r3_uri
R3 Document Access Restriction, line 729: the AS fetching r3_uri MUST sign as a server in its own right, under jwks_uri with id set to its issuer and aauth-access.json
Issuer Processing, step 3, line 547: if the bytes the AS received do not hash to r3_s256, the issuer MUST reject the Resource token; no Auth token reaches the agent

Issuer Processing, step 6 (line 550), and Auth Token Extensions, lines 569-571: the AS-issued Auth token MUST include the document's r3_uri and r3_s256 and r3_granted, whose operations are drawn from that document (line 617)

R3 Document Access Restriction, lines 729 and 734: in four-party access the PS also fetches, and a party fetching r3_uri MUST sign as itself under jwks_uri (aauth-person.json); not exercised when the PS makes no fetch
Hash Verification, line 740: a party that fetches an R3 document MUST verify r3_s256 against it before using it; a PS served bytes that do not match gives no Auth token

Mission Approval line 1412 (s256 REQUIRED: unpadded base64url SHA-256 of the bytes mission decodes to) and Mission Identifier line 1437 (the PS MUST compute s256 over the exact bytes it returns as mission)
Mission Approval, line 1413: mission is REQUIRED, the mission blob base64url-encoded without padding
Mission Approval, lines 1417-1421: the mission blob MUST include agent, approved_at (ISO 8601) and description
Mission Identifier, line 1437: the PS MUST serve the same mission bytes wherever it later exposes the mission (graded only where the PS exposes it to the owner)

Person Token Endpoint, line 810: the PS MUST verify the named mission exists, is active and belongs to this agent, and MUST reject the request otherwise (invalid_request for a malformed mission_s256, line 840)

Person Token Structure, line 863: a person token MUST NOT outlive the mission's expires_at when mission_s256 is present
Mission Approval, line 1425: every PS decision path that acts on a mission MUST treat a mission past expires_at as terminated
Mission Management, line 1514: for a terminated mission the PS MUST reject requests with mission_terminated
Mission Management, line 1516: a terminated mission MUST NOT return to active
Mission Status Errors, lines 1550-1565: a request to any PS endpoint naming a mission that is no longer active MUST get the error: 403, error mission_terminated, mission_status terminated
Mission Endpoint Errors, line 1540: a PS MUST return the same status, error, body and header set whether the mission does not exist or the agent does not own it (timing is not graded)
Resource Token Verification, line 768: if mission_s256 is present a PS MUST verify the mission is active and the current time precedes its expires_at
